npcs.name: Farseer Nakhtar
npcs.greeting: Prove yourself against the beasts of this valley, and Orgrimmar will open its gates to you.

npcs.name: Valley Grunt
npcs.greeting: Keep your blade sharp. The scorpid don't wait for you to finish talking.

npcs.name: Elder Kuraw
npcs.greeting: The Horde was not given to us. We built it. Remember that when it gets hard.

npcs.name: Durotar Sentry
npcs.greeting: Move along. The road to Razor Hill is clear, but keep your eyes open past the ridge.

npcs.name: Grosk the Wanderer
npcs.greeting: Sand in my boots, sun on my back. Wouldn't trade this life for Orgrimmar's walls.

npcs.name: Grukk's Son
npcs.greeting: Someday I'll fight with the Warsong! Watch, I'll show you my sparring stance!

npcs.name: Razor Hill Grunt
npcs.greeting: Razor Hill holds the line between the valley and the capital. It always has.

npcs.name: Blacksmith Kragg
npcs.greeting: Bring me ore and I'll turn it into something that bites back.

npcs.name: Grizzik
npcs.greeting: Ships in, goods out, coin changes hands. That's Ratchet.

npcs.name: Salty Pete
npcs.greeting: Neutral port, they say. Neutral just means everybody's watching everybody.

npcs.name: Fizzle Brassbolt
npcs.greeting: Everything has a price in Ratchet. Everything.

npcs.name: Tarna Swiftwave
npcs.greeting: The reef here runs deep with fish and deeper with old bones. Careful where you wade.

npcs.name: Spiritwalker Kesh
npcs.greeting: The spirits of these isles remember when they were free. Tread with respect.

npcs.name: Camp Sentry
npcs.greeting: Camp Taurajo stands. It has stood through worse than you.

npcs.name: Elder Longtread
npcs.greeting: The land remembers every herd that has passed through it. We are only passing too.

npcs.name: Crossroads Grunt
npcs.greeting: The Crossroads sees every caravan between the coasts. Someone has to keep it standing.

npcs.name: Wandering Vendor
npcs.greeting: Passing through. Always passing through. That's the Barrens for you.

npcs.name: Herder Magra Dustwalker
npcs.greeting: Kodo don't rush for anyone. Neither do I, out here.

npcs.name: Plainswatcher Dorn
npcs.greeting: You can see a sandstorm coming an hour out here. Can't always outrun it.

npcs.name: Weapons Trainer Grokk
npcs.greeting: Come back when your arm is tired of swinging. That's when the real training starts.

npcs.name: Innkeeper Grosk
npcs.greeting: Rest here a while. The road to Orgrimmar is long and Durotar doesn't forgive tired feet.

npcs.name: Forsaken Guardsman
npcs.greeting: The Dark Lady watches over this city. Mind your business and she'll mind hers.

npcs.name: Apothecary Marwen
npcs.greeting: Plague research isn't for the squeamish. Neither is Undercity, come to that.

npcs.name: Loremaster Sennarath
npcs.greeting: I came to the Undercity for the archives, not the company. Though the company grows on you.

npcs.name: Grukthar Deepdweller
npcs.greeting: An orc, in Undercity? The Horde is stranger and stronger for it. I go where the coin goes.

npcs.name: Tirisfal Watcher
npcs.greeting: The fog rolls thick through these woods. It hides more than it should.

npcs.name: Forsaken Peasant
npcs.greeting: We were people once. Some days I still remember what that felt like.

npcs.name: Brill Guardsman
npcs.greeting: Brill stands between Undercity and the living lands. We don't let much through uninvited.

npcs.name: Old Farmer Nettles
npcs.greeting: Still tend the fields, even now. Habits die harder than people do, it turns out.

npcs.name: Death Knight Instructor
npcs.greeting: You wake in a graveyard with no memory of dying. Welcome to the Forsaken. It gets easier.

npcs.name: Newly Risen
npcs.greeting: I don't- I don't remember my name yet. Give it time, they said.

npcs.name: Silverpine Scout
npcs.greeting: Worgen prowl these woods some nights. Keep to the road after dark.

npcs.name: Forsaken Hunter
npcs.greeting: Even death didn't stop me from putting meat on the table. Old habits.

npcs.name: Grulnok
npcs.greeting: You'll want to keep an eye on the ridge line. Boars don't usually wander this close to the fire.

npcs.name: Fizzcrank Sprocketspin
npcs.greeting: Don't touch that. It's not finished. It also might be a little bit on fire.

npcs.name: Rhaka
npcs.greeting: My son went up the ridge to prove himself last week. He came back. That's all I ask of this place.

npcs.name: Torgak
npcs.greeting: Scorpid got me good before I put it down. Nakhtar says I'll live. I believe her more than I believe my leg.

npcs.name: Unmoving Remains
npcs.greeting: It doesn't move. It doesn't speak. Someone should probably ask the Farseer why it's just... standing there.

npcs.name: Grosk the Younger
npcs.greeting: Someday I'm going to walk out of this valley and never look back at the boars again.

npcs.name: Razor Hill Sentry
npcs.greeting: Watch the north road. That's where trouble comes from, when it comes at all.

npcs.name: Razor Hill Sentry
npcs.greeting: You've got the look of someone fresh out of the Valley. Try not to die on your first walk through town.

npcs.name: Kravel Coinsnatch
npcs.greeting: Everything has a price, friend. Even the conversation. Just kidding. Mostly.

npcs.name: Aendel Duskrunner
npcs.greeting: I keep the Horde's ledgers here. Someone has to. It certainly isn't going to be the orcs.

npcs.name: Corlan Ashe
npcs.greeting: I stopped believing in the Alliance's version of things a long time ago. The Horde took me in when nobody else would.

npcs.name: Kagra
npcs.greeting: The soil out here fights you for every root vegetable. I've learned to fight back harder.

npcs.name: Little Snarl
npcs.greeting: When I grow up I'm going to kill a whole cave full of demons by myself. Just watch.

npcs.name: Grandmother Ulaka
npcs.greeting: I remember when this hill had nothing on it but wind and bones. Look at it now. We built something.

npcs.name: Prizzle Boltwrench
npcs.greeting: I've got seven inventions in various states of exploding. Statistically, one of them will work eventually.

npcs.name: Orgrimmar Outrider
npcs.greeting: The gates of Orgrimmar are close now. Prove yourself worthy before you reach them.

npcs.name: Ridgewatch Kurr
npcs.greeting: Thunder lizards up on the ridge. Slow, but they hit like the ground opening up under you.

npcs.name: Skull Rock Watcher
npcs.greeting: Something's wrong out past those rocks. Been wrong for longer than I've been posted here.

npcs.name: Gazlowe's Cousin Fitz
npcs.greeting: There's a fortune in this dirt somewhere. I just haven't found the exact spot yet. Or any spot, honestly.

npcs.name: Borka the Watchful
npcs.greeting: The quilboar camp's grown bigger since the thaw. Someone ought to do something about that. Maybe you.

npcs.name: Sunbleached Remains
npcs.greeting: Whoever this was, the desert took the rest of the story with them.

npcs.name: Sylthressa Windmourne
npcs.greeting: I travel between Razor Hill and the coast. Durotar's rough country, but the profit margins are excellent.

npcs.name: Wyll Marrow
npcs.greeting: I was Alliance once. Then I was a prisoner. Now I'm just someone who chose to stay. Funny how that happens.

npcs.name: Southbound Grekka
npcs.greeting: Heading down to the Valley to see my nephew off. First trial. Nervous doesn't cover it.

npcs.name: Wandering Bok
npcs.greeting: Road's clear between here and Razor Hill. Mostly. There was a thing with a vulture yesterday. Don't ask.

npcs.name: Talra Saltbraid
npcs.greeting: The nets don't mend themselves, and the sea doesn't care that my hands ache.

npcs.name: Kelp-Diver Muzka
npcs.greeting: I can hold my breath longer than anyone on this isle. Ask anyone. Well - ask anyone who's still speaking to me.

npcs.name: Reef Wrangler Dritt
npcs.greeting: There's a wreck off the north shore worth more than this whole island. I just need a boat. And a crew. And a plan.

npcs.name: Elder Tidecaller Vashj
npcs.greeting: The spirits of this isle remember when it belonged to no one and everyone. Walk gently.

npcs.name: Drowned Remains
npcs.greeting: Whatever ship this washed off of, it isn't coming back for the rest.

npcs.name: Watchwarden Kelgrim
npcs.greeting: The ruins are quiet today. Doesn't mean they're safe. It never does.

npcs.name: Bloodwarden Ashgrym
npcs.greeting: The Burning Blade doesn't die easy. I've been trying for longer than I care to say.

npcs.name: Jin'zil
npcs.greeting: Dis island remember more than da orcs who live on it now, mon. Da spirits still talk, if you know how to listen.

npcs.name: Zathra Voodoo-Eye
npcs.greeting: You bleedin'? No? Den come back when you are. I don't do idle chat, mon, I do mendin'.

npcs.name: Elder Kang'ari
npcs.greeting: My people wandered long before we washed up here. Da orcs gave us a place to stop wanderin'. Dat's worth somethin', mon.

npcs.name: Rask'jin
npcs.greeting: Camp don't build itself, mon. You want to help, dere's always somethin' need gatherin'.

npcs.name: Vessa Palewind
npcs.greeting: I watch da tree line. Somethin' move wrong out dere, I see it before it sees you.

npcs.name: Tal'rashi
npcs.greeting: I made it dis far. Not everyone did. Not everyone still trapped out dere will, either.

npcs.name: Caravan Guard Dresk
npcs.greeting: Caravans in and out all day. Someone's got to make sure they all still have their wheels.

npcs.name: Quartermaster Ruka
npcs.greeting: Every warband passing through gets counted, armed, and sent on their way. That's the job.

npcs.name: Message Runner Kol
npcs.greeting: Can't talk long. Orgrimmar needs this by nightfall and my legs don't fly.

npcs.name: Old Grukan
npcs.greeting: Board's full of bounties nobody's fool enough to take. Except you, maybe.

npcs.name: One-Eye Thokk
npcs.greeting: Lost the eye at Ashenvale. Lost the taste for fighting somewhere after that.

npcs.name: Snix Cogsworth
npcs.greeting: Trinkets, baubles, one careful lady owned it! Well - one careful goblin.

npcs.name: Envoy Thaelis
npcs.greeting: Silvermoon sends its regards to the Horde. And its curiosity about this... dust.

npcs.name: Corwin Hale
npcs.greeting: Long way from Stormwind. Longer way back, I suspect. But the Horde's been fair to me.

npcs.name: Little Ugak
npcs.greeting: I counted eleven caravans today! Ma says I'm not allowed to count the goblin ones anymore.

npcs.name: Windrunner Kala
npcs.greeting: The kodo herds moved south early this year. Something's stirring in the Southern Barrens.

npcs.name: Carver Ahonen
npcs.greeting: Each totem holds a spirit's promise. Carve it wrong and the promise breaks.

npcs.name: Tanner Mosswalker
npcs.greeting: A kodo gives its hide once it's done giving everything else. We waste nothing here.

npcs.name: Drum-Keeper Rohan
npcs.greeting: The war drums haven't sounded in a generation. I keep them ready all the same.

npcs.name: Wrangler Tull
npcs.greeting: Kodo don't spook easy, but when they do, get out of the way. All of it.

npcs.name: Little Rundu
npcs.greeting: Grandmother says I'll be tall as the totem pole someday. I hope it's soon.

npcs.name: Scout Ashhoof
npcs.greeting: Centaur activity's up near Bael Modan. Camp's on watch until it settles.

npcs.name: Liaison Grukdar
npcs.greeting: Orgrimmar sends grain, the Tauren send warriors. Fair trade, if you ask me.

npcs.name: Earthsong Mara
npcs.greeting: The earth remembers every wound. It's just a matter of asking it to forget.

npcs.name: Gravedigger Hollis
npcs.greeting: Digging graves is slower work now that most of what's in them gets up and walks away.

npcs.name: Assistant Grael
npcs.greeting: The Apothecarium doesn't share what it's brewing. I just carry the crates and don't ask.

npcs.name: Crier Wexley
npcs.greeting: Hear ye! The Dark Lady's will is the Forsaken's will! Also, the well needs fixing again.

npcs.name: Farmhand Joss
npcs.greeting: I still remember planting these fields. Funny what the mind keeps, after.

npcs.name: Meryl Ashdown
npcs.greeting: My sister's one of them now. I stayed to make sure someone still calls her by name.

npcs.name: Trader Ilvessa
npcs.greeting: Silvermoon's reagent trade runs through here more than people realize.

npcs.name: Bell-Ringer Ohmsted
npcs.greeting: The bell doesn't call the living to worship anymore. Just marks the hours. Same difference.

npcs.name: Old Pruit
npcs.greeting: Scarecrows scare the crows just fine. It's the other things that don't scare so easy.

npcs.name: Deathguard Rennick
npcs.greeting: Balnir Farmstead's had trouble again. Worgen, or something wearing a worgen's shape.

npcs.name: Tomb-Keeper Ellowyn
npcs.greeting: Every tomb here held someone's name, once. I try to remember them, since no one else will.

npcs.name: The Mourner
npcs.greeting: I don't remember who I'm mourning. I just know I haven't stopped.

npcs.name: Relic Hunter Darne
npcs.greeting: These crypts predate the Scourge. Whatever's buried down there, it isn't ours to wake.

npcs.name: Crypt Guard Molsen
npcs.greeting: Nothing gets in or out of the lower vaults. Not while I stand here.

npcs.name: The Hermit
npcs.greeting: Go away. Or stay, I suppose. It's been quiet here a long time either way.

npcs.name: Bone-Carver Yseult
npcs.greeting: I carve what the tombs give up. Some of it's art. Most of it's just a warning.

npcs.name: Wandering Pilgrim Osk
npcs.greeting: I walk from tomb to tomb. I couldn't tell you why. Maybe I'm looking for my own.

npcs.name: Reader Cass
npcs.greeting: Half these stones are worn smooth. I read them anyway. Someone should.

npcs.name: Fishmonger Gribble
npcs.greeting: Fresh catch, fresher prices! Well - fresh catch. The prices are Ratchet prices.

npcs.name: Smuggler Fintan
npcs.greeting: I don't know what's in the crates. I never ask. Long career built on never asking.

npcs.name: Laborer Hask
npcs.greeting: Ships don't unload themselves. Wish they did. My back's had enough.

npcs.name: Bounty Hunter Drask
npcs.greeting: Neutral port means neutral money. I'll take a contract from either side, or both.

npcs.name: Barnacle Bill
npcs.greeting: Ship left without me. Again. Third time this month, I think. Or this week.

npcs.name: Customs Officer Prynn
npcs.greeting: Neutral ground, official rules. Declare your cargo or don't - I get paid either way.

npcs.name: Little Gribs
npcs.greeting: I'm gonna build a boat that goes faster than the zeppelin! You'll see!

npcs.name: Delia Thorne
npcs.greeting: Stormwind's politics got old. Ratchet's simpler - everyone's just here for the money.

npcs.name: Zulraka
npcs.greeting: Echo Isles to Ratchet and back, every week. Good pay for a strong back.

npcs.name: Outrider Kelsara
npcs.greeting: Far Watch Post holds the eastern road. Has since before I got here, will after I'm gone too.

npcs.name: Warsong Outrider Dask
npcs.greeting: Warsong Outriders don't rest easy this far from Orgrimmar. Neither should you.

npcs.name: Kranal Fiss
npcs.greeting: Grol'dom's held since before Orgrimmar had proper walls. Quilboar press us from both sides some seasons, but the pigs don't care and neither do I.

npcs.name: Elder Torgun
npcs.greeting: The Horde was not given to us. We built it. Remember that when it gets hard.

npcs.name: Kardris Dreamseeker
npcs.greeting: The elemental spirits of this place have sent out a summons for a shaman of your wisdom. Come speak with me.

npcs.name: Rethok the Hunter
npcs.greeting: The wilds beyond Durotar don't forgive mistakes. Learn that here, where it's safer to be wrong.

npcs.name: Kranok Wildmane
npcs.greeting: Wolves, boars, the occasional stubborn raptor. I've broken all of them to the saddle eventually.

npcs.name: Zathyra Duskweave
npcs.greeting: Magic isn't given, it's taken - from the raw stuff of the world, carefully, or it takes something back.

npcs.name: Voren Glimmerhand
npcs.greeting: Bring me a blade and I'll make it remember what it's for.

npcs.name: Krunk Anvilfist
npcs.greeting: Bring me ore and I'll turn it into something that bites back.

npcs.name: Grommash's Shadow
npcs.greeting: Strength isn't the absence of fear. It's fighting on past it. Every warrior learns that the hard way.

npcs.name: Dutmar Ironjaw
npcs.greeting: A dull blade is a liability. Bring yours to me before it gets you killed.

npcs.name: Malzhet the Bound
npcs.greeting: Power always costs something. The question is only ever whether you're willing to pay it.

npcs.name: Yura Emberveil
npcs.greeting: Summon carelessly and something comes through that you didn't call. Ask me how I know.

npcs.name: Apothecary Zurm
npcs.greeting: Zurm's brews. Good for what ails you, mostly. Don't ask about the rest.

npcs.name: Shade of Thalorien
npcs.greeting: You won't see me coming. That's the whole point.

npcs.name: Vexia Nightshade
npcs.greeting: Fast-acting, slow-acting, undetectable. I stock all three, and I don't ask what you need it for.

npcs.name: Brewmaster Tolga
npcs.greeting: Every potion's a promise. Mine keep theirs.

npcs.name: Sarnda Hidecraft
npcs.greeting: Bring me hide, I'll bring you armor. Bring me good hide, I'll bring you armor worth wearing.

npcs.name: Ilyenne Threadweave
npcs.greeting: Cloth doesn't stop a blade. It stops the cold, though, and that kills just as many people eventually.

npcs.name: Grosk Wolfrider
npcs.greeting: Every orc worth the name rides a wolf. I make sure they're worth the name.

npcs.name: Kessa Trailrunner
npcs.greeting: Feed, water, rest. Same three things every mount needs, same three things half the riders forget.

npcs.name: Ragnok Packmule
npcs.greeting: Rope, saddlebags, feed sacks. Not glamorous. Everyone needs it eventually.

npcs.name: Windrider Master Kar
npcs.greeting: Wind's good today. You want to fly, now's the time to ask.

npcs.name: Grokka Fireforge
npcs.greeting: Grokka Fireforge's stall. If it's worth having, I've probably got it - or I know who does.

npcs.name: Cook Bragok
npcs.greeting: Roasted meat, fresh bread. A warband marches on a full stomach, not empty promises.

npcs.name: Nara Greenroot
npcs.greeting: Herbs from every corner of Kalimdor pass through this stall eventually. Ask, and I'll probably have it.

npcs.name: Old Salt Kelgar
npcs.greeting: Fresh off the boat from Ratchet this morning. Won't stay fresh forever, so don't dawdle.

npcs.name: Bela Quickpelt
npcs.greeting: Barrens hide, Ashenvale fur, the occasional oddity from further out. Something for every coin purse.

npcs.name: Wexil Inkfeather
npcs.greeting: Scrolls, contracts, letters home. Whatever needs writing, I can write it - for a price.

npcs.name: Curio Trader Ashna
npcs.greeting: Trinkets, oddities, the occasional genuine relic. I sort the real from the fake, mostly.

npcs.name: Doughmaster Fennel
npcs.greeting: Fresh bread, fresh every morning. Rain or shine or centaur raid, I bake.

npcs.name: Petal Windgrace
npcs.greeting: Not every stall in Orgrimmar needs to sell steel. Some of us sell things that just make it prettier.

npcs.name: Kesh Farflavor
npcs.greeting: Spices from Stranglethorn to the Barrens, all in one stall. Taste before you buy.

npcs.name: Tinker Sprocket
npcs.greeting: Clockwork toys, harmless little gadgets. Mostly harmless. Read the label.

npcs.name: Sagorne Creststrider
npcs.greeting: The Earthmother watches over all who seek her wisdom here.

npcs.name: Thrall
npcs.greeting: Lok'tar ogar. The Horde endures because we endure.

npcs.name: Gazlowe
npcs.greeting: Everything's for sale, friend. Even the things that aren't.

npcs.name: Sergra Darkthorn
npcs.greeting: Keep your head down and your business quick. The Crossroads doesn't run itself.

npcs.name: Sentinel Eltharaen
npcs.greeting: Ashenvale bleeds a little more each day. Stay armed, stay watchful.

npcs.name: Talonar Swiftmoon
npcs.greeting: The moon watches over Astranaar tonight, as it always has.

npcs.name: Innkeeper Rimble
npcs.greeting: Rest here a while, traveler. Ashenvale's roads aren't kind after dark.

npcs.name: Kerlonian Evershade
npcs.greeting: The wild whispers to those who know how to listen. Do you?

npcs.name: Sentinel Drill Instructor
npcs.greeting: Form up. Ashenvale doesn't forgive sloppy footwork.

npcs.name: Astranaar Flight Master
npcs.greeting: Where do you need to fly, friend?

npcs.name: Overseer Gorada
npcs.greeting: The demons don't sleep, and neither do we. What do you need?

npcs.name: Barracks Sergeant Krull
npcs.greeting: Every warrior we send north comes back changed, if they come back at all.

npcs.name: Watch Sentry Mokka
npcs.greeting: Quiet tonight. Too quiet, if you ask me.

npcs.name: Outpost Guard
npcs.greeting: Move along unless you've got business here.

npcs.name: Scout Veyra
npcs.greeting: I've seen things past that treeline I can't unsee.

npcs.name: Splintertree Flight Master
npcs.greeting: Where do you need to fly, friend?

npcs.name: Sentinel Maestra
npcs.greeting: The furbolg in the Highlands used to leave us be. Something's turned them, and I mean to find out what.

npcs.name: Sentinel Shalasyr
npcs.greeting: Eltharaen keeps the hall standing. I keep the roads open. Lately that's the harder job.

npcs.name: Grove Warden Pennarin
npcs.greeting: Moonwhisper Grove answers to no one, but even a sanctuary needs watching when the wilds turn strange.

npcs.name: Thessaly Windrunner
npcs.greeting: We ran from the east coast with nothing. If I could just get a few things back, I could start again.

npcs.name: War Mage Grimtotem
npcs.greeting: Gorada holds the command tent. I hold the line at Satyr's Throne. Neither of us sleeps much.

npcs.name: Grunt Bloodfang
npcs.greeting: The Wastes used to just be scorched dirt. Now things crawl out of it at night.

npcs.name: Interrogator Vashj
npcs.greeting: Every satyr we drag out of the Barrow swears the void is close to breaking through. I'd like to know how close.

npcs.name: Overseer Krell
npcs.greeting: You've got a body and a grudge against the living. That's enough to start with. I've got work.

npcs.name: Scout Hollowmere
npcs.greeting: The Scarlet Crusade thinks burning us twice makes it stick. They're welcome to try again.

npcs.name: Watcher Pell
npcs.greeting: Cold Hearth Manor used to house the living. Now it just houses what's left of them, badly.

npcs.name: Keeper Oswin
npcs.greeting: Raven Hill's dead don't always stay that way. I've buried the same corpse three times this month.

npcs.name: Warden Yaelis
npcs.greeting: The Shadowspring used to be sweet. Now it runs black, and the things that drink from it run hungry.

npcs.name: Sergeant Dallow
npcs.greeting: The March exists to keep the road to Ambermill open. Lately that's a full-time fight.

npcs.name: Elder Gravemoss
npcs.greeting: Bloodmoon Village is the only safe ground left on this island, and even that's generous.

npcs.name: Huntsman Corwell
npcs.greeting: Baron Ashbury ruled this isle alive and he rules it worse dead. Someone needs to finish what the curse started.

npcs.name: Waterkeeper Sanu Goldenhoof
npcs.greeting: The water remembers every traveller. I only try to keep it from remembering the wrong ones.

npcs.name: Pilgrim-Warden Torga
npcs.greeting: They came to pray and they never went home. Someone should still be here to hear them.

npcs.name: Caravan-Master Dogan Ironcart
npcs.greeting: Raider's Rest has water, shade and a fair price on everything. The bandits do not like the third one.

npcs.name: Keeper Ahnmar Stonetotem
npcs.greeting: Quiet, friend. The stone is listening, and so, I think, is the one who fell.

npcs.name: Scout Zarla Blackthorn
npcs.greeting: Keep your voice down. The cult has ears in the rocks, and I'd like to keep the one I have left.

npcs.name: Ranger Kishi Plainstalker
npcs.greeting: Boars to the left, boars to the right, and a road down the middle. It's a pleasant walk, if you like arguing.

npcs.name: Bridgewarden Karga Redfang
npcs.greeting: Southfury bridge, Barrens end. Every plank paid for in blood and bad weather. Mind your step.

npcs.name: Rift-Warden Brakka Stonehoof
npcs.greeting: Everything south of here is the Rift's business. Everything north of it is mine. Try to keep them separate.

npcs.name: Bonehunter Rurk Gravetusk
npcs.greeting: Giants walked this plain once. Now it's bones, hyenas and me. I'm the only one who likes the company.

npcs.name: Thornwatch Ranger Oggra
npcs.greeting: Quilboar to the south, quilboar to the north, and one very annoyed ranger in the middle. Don't stand near my fire.

npcs.name: Spy Zhuul Quicksight
npcs.greeting: Keep your voice low, mon. Dem dwarves have good ears and bad tempers.

npcs.name: Dig-Scout Tarrik Ashmane
npcs.greeting: Quarry's loud, the dwarves are louder, and the pit keeps getting deeper. I don't like it.

npcs.name: Huntress Alamir Bloodtotem
npcs.greeting: Stay low in the spires. The wind carries voices out there, and some of them are not the wind's.

npcs.name: Excavator Fizzwick Boltcog
npcs.greeting: Fizzwick Boltcog, licensed excavator! Okay, not licensed. Okay, not an excavator. But I know a hole when I see one.

npcs.name: Road-Warden Hargak Ironvein
npcs.greeting: Gold Road, my road, my rules. Pay the toll, or don't. Bandits do the second one and I'd rather you didn't.

npcs.name: Beachmaster Kizzle Fuseblast
npcs.greeting: Welcome to the Merchant Coast! Mind the crabs, the pirates and the cannon. In that order.

npcs.name: Scout Mahri Dustwalker
npcs.greeting: Don't drink the water. I wish I were joking. The hounds don't care, but they're not as picky as you.

npcs.name: Captain Korvash Gatebreaker
npcs.greeting: Behind me, the Rampart. In front of me, the Kaldorei. Between us, you. Choose a side quickly.

npcs.name: Huntress Zan'ula Skyshard
npcs.greeting: Hush, mon. The hills have ears and the Witchwings have eyes. Mostly eyes. Mostly hungry.

npcs.name: Earthcaller Rohna Skyhorn
npcs.greeting: The earth is crying out, child. It isn't a happy cry. I'd like you to make it stop.

npcs.name: Fenwarden Dugmok Mudhoof
npcs.greeting: Everything in the fen is slow, wet and hungry. Welcome. You'll fit right in.

npcs.name: Salvager Nix Cogsprocket
npcs.greeting: I used to work for the Venture Company. Used to. Now I watch them work, from a safe distance. With a very large wrench.

npcs.name: Claim-Surveyor Gruda Deepdelve
npcs.greeting: The Lode's ours by right and by paperwork. The Company has the pickaxes. I have the stubborn.

npcs.name: Innkeeper Gryshka
npcs.greeting: Beds are clean, ale is cold, and nobody asks where you got the blood on your boots. Want me to be your hearth?

npcs.name: Riding Instructor Zhurak
npcs.greeting: Sit tall, lean into the turn, and never show a wolf you're afraid. Ready to learn?

npcs.name: Windrider Master Zhaka
npcs.greeting: The wyverns are fed and the wind is fair. Where to?

npcs.name: Innkeeper Boorka
npcs.greeting: Cots in the back, stew in the front. Bind your hearth here and the Barrens can't lose you.

npcs.name: Windrider Master Hurak
npcs.greeting: The Crossroads is the busiest roost on the continent. Name a destination.

npcs.name: Riding Instructor Vash'ka
npcs.greeting: Raptors, wolves, kodo - it all comes down to who's in charge. Let me show you.

npcs.name: Ratchet Windrider Zibb
npcs.greeting: Fastest wyvern in the harbour. Cheap, too, if you don't count the screaming.

npcs.name: Innkeeper Mahkra
npcs.greeting: Rest easy, traveller. The earth mother watches over this hearth.

npcs.name: Windrider Master Kaya
npcs.greeting: The winds carry word and wings alike. Where shall they take you?

npcs.name: Riding Instructor Tull Greyhoof
npcs.greeting: A kodo carries you if you carry yourself right. Let me teach you.

npcs.name: Innkeeper Rukka
npcs.greeting: Even a war camp needs a hot meal. Bind your hearth and fight easier.

npcs.name: Innkeeper Doda Longhorn
npcs.greeting: The Waystation's cots are narrow and the soup is mostly soup. Bind here?

npcs.name: Windrider Master Orga
npcs.greeting: The canyon's too wide to walk and too wide to jump. Fly with me.

npcs.name: Boatwright Illyen
npcs.greeting: The Strand's boats go where the tide lets them. Mind the planks, they're wet.

npcs.name: Old Maelis
npcs.greeting: Silverfin run thick this season. Shame the Horde ships scare them off.

npcs.name: Lookout Taelanor
npcs.greeting: I watch the water so the others can sleep. Nothing has crossed it tonight.

npcs.name: Foreman Gruzak
npcs.greeting: Axes up, you lot! ... Oh. You're not one of mine. Well, don't just stand there, there's wood to cut.

npcs.name: Warden Aelyndra
npcs.greeting: Quiet, please. This is a place for grief, and you are not the first to bring noise.

npcs.name: Foreman Gresk
npcs.greeting: Don't touch the shaft. Don't touch the crew. Don't touch the spiders. Actually - do touch the spiders.

npcs.name: Mourner Isolde
npcs.greeting: The water's cold. It is always cold. I keep thinking if I sit here long enough, it will stop.

npcs.name: Gardener Orrel
npcs.greeting: Nothing grows here. I know. I plant anyway. Somebody has to believe in tomorrow.

npcs.name: Scout Verrick
npcs.greeting: Keep your voice down. The Scarlets have good ears and short tempers.

npcs.name: Sexton Marrow
npcs.greeting: Every soul deserves a proper burial. Even the ones that won't stay in it.

npcs.name: Ranger Corvin Ashe
npcs.greeting: Keep to the road. The Vale doesn't like surprises, and neither do I.

npcs.name: Fisher Quillon
npcs.greeting: Nothing bites any more. Except the Vile Fins, and they bite with spears.

npcs.name: Scout Dessa Vane
npcs.greeting: Quiet. The Crusade has sharp eyes and a short list of things it forgives.

npcs.name: Widow Marren
npcs.greeting: The fields are all that's left. I tend them. I don't know why.

npcs.name: Hermit Oswin
npcs.greeting: I came for the quiet. The pond has opinions about that.

npcs.name: Envoy Sorren
npcs.greeting: Brill sends me to ask politely. After that, it sends you.

npcs.name: Keeper Halvard
npcs.greeting: The family's dead and they won't stay quiet about it.

npcs.name: Warden Brask
npcs.greeting: Garren's Haunt has always had gnolls. Lately it has more.

npcs.name: Deathguard Linnea
npcs.greeting: Passengers to the left, ropes to the right, ghosts directly overhead.

npcs.name: Gravekeeper Morvyn
npcs.greeting: They don't stay down any more. Not in Faol's Rest.

npcs.name: Warden Gunther Lorn
npcs.greeting: The lake's watching you. It watches everyone.

npcs.name: Scout Hallam
npcs.greeting: Keep low. They've got archers on the wall.

npcs.name: Huntress Ravel
npcs.greeting: The Vale eats the careless. Mind your step.

npcs.name: Stablehand Edric
npcs.greeting: The horses are gone. The stable remains. So do I.

npcs.name: Warden Ysolde Grave
npcs.greeting: I came here to watch. Now I count.

npcs.name: Boneward Calder
npcs.greeting: That hole behind the farm breathes. Don't tell me it doesn't.

npcs.name: Deathguard Halloran
npcs.greeting: Keep to the avenue. The canal is not for swimming, and I'm tired of fishing out tourists.

npcs.name: MerchantTusk
npcs.greeting: Dere is only one bank, mon, and dere is only one me. Do not ask how dat works. Hand me ya things and go be a hero.

npcs.name: Auctioneer Dross
npcs.greeting: Going once, going twice... going to the lady with the suspiciously large coin purse!

npcs.name: Mortician Gravelle
npcs.greeting: Business is slow. Strange, for an undertaker, in a city of the dead.

npcs.name: Embalmer Pell
npcs.greeting: Preservative salts, wax, and thread. Everything a body needs to keep its shape.

npcs.name: Cook Marrowbone
npcs.greeting: Taste is optional down here. Nutrition, I'm told, is merely a habit.

npcs.name: Herbalist Thistledown
npcs.greeting: Grave-moss, deadnettle, a little foxglove. Nothing here will kill you. Probably.

npcs.name: Scribe Ormsby
npcs.greeting: Letters of passage, last wills, and the occasional love note. Don't ask which is which.

npcs.name: Tailor Yarrow
npcs.greeting: Burial shrouds, travelling cloaks, whatever you can stitch from a sheet. Hems are free.

npcs.name: Relic-Hunter Crane
npcs.greeting: Everything you see was found somewhere it shouldn't have been. That's what makes it valuable.

npcs.name: Butcher Grimsby
npcs.greeting: Fresh as the day it was... well. Fresh as it gets. Don't ask.

npcs.name: Lady Sylvanas Windrunner
npcs.greeting: The Horde stands with the Forsaken. Prove yourself worthy of that trust, and you shall not regret it.

npcs.name: Royal Guard Ashworth
npcs.greeting: The Banshee Queen receives only those who have earned the audience. State your business.

npcs.name: Royal Guard Venn
npcs.greeting: Eyes front. Weapons sheathed. Breathing is optional, but quiet is not.

npcs.name: Executor Wrenfall
npcs.greeting: The Dark Lady's will does not wait. If you've the stomach for real work, I have it.

npcs.name: Deathstalker Rhyne
npcs.greeting: If you can see me, I wanted you to. Keep that in mind.

npcs.name: Magistrix Valdis
npcs.greeting: Frost, fire, arcane. The grave is cold, so I've a certain appreciation for frost.

npcs.name: Dreadmaster Kol'ven
npcs.greeting: The Burning Legion bargains for souls. I have learned to drive a harder deal.

npcs.name: Dark Cleric Beryl
npcs.greeting: Shadow does not mean evil. It means honest about the dark. Come, learn.

npcs.name: Summoner Aldric Voss
npcs.greeting: Stand within the circle, and not one foot beyond. The last apprentice learned that the hard way.

npcs.name: Enchantress Maeve Dunmoor
npcs.greeting: Bring me your best blade and a bad attitude. I'll improve one of the two.

npcs.name: Battlemaster Grakk
npcs.greeting: Strength isn't built from comfort. Pick up a weapon and show me you're not afraid of bruises.

npcs.name: Ranger Isolde
npcs.greeting: Every hunter learns patience. The dead just learn it sooner.

npcs.name: Beastmaster Kovach
npcs.greeting: The bat doesn't mind that you're dead. That's why I trust it more than most people.

npcs.name: Shadowblade Kess
npcs.greeting: Quiet feet, quiet blades. If I hear you coming, we start over.

npcs.name: Smith Ironbrow
npcs.greeting: The forge is still hot. That's more than I can say for myself.

npcs.name: Weaponsmith Torvald
npcs.greeting: A good edge lasts. I'd know. I've held mine for forty years past dying.

npcs.name: Drillmaster Hask
npcs.greeting: Again! The Scourge won't wait for you to catch your breath.

npcs.name: Master Apothecary Lorrane Sable
npcs.greeting: Some of my own Society have turned their craft on the Dark Lady. The vaults below are theirs now. I want them cleaned out, and I want the ringleaders brought to account.

npcs.name: Alchemist Dunmere
npcs.greeting: Stir clockwise. Always clockwise. The one time I didn't, I lost an arm. Again.

npcs.name: Surgeon Halvard
npcs.greeting: Hold still. I do my best work on patients who are already past the screaming.

npcs.name: Lab Assistant Pip
npcs.greeting: Don't touch the green one. Or the blue one. Or the one that looks like jam.

npcs.name: Gatewarden Sorrel
npcs.greeting: Beyond the gate lie the Plague Depths, and a cabal of Apothecary traitors who want the Dark Lady dead. If you hear screaming down there, it isn't mine.

npcs.name: Deathguard Marik
npcs.greeting: Nobody's gone through that gate who wasn't ordered to. Remember that when you feel brave.

npcs.name: Riding Instructor Cask
npcs.greeting: A skeletal horse is a patient steed. It will carry you forever, and it will never complain about the road.

npcs.name: Captain Hollin Vesk
npcs.greeting: Welcome to the Rear Guard. We hold the gate so the Sepulcher can pretend the north is quiet.

npcs.name: Apothecary Pell
npcs.greeting: Don't touch the cauldron. Don't breathe the cauldron. Look at it from a distance, if you must.

npcs.name: Dark Cleric Ravenna
npcs.greeting: The Light never answered us. The Dark has, at least. It prefers prayers in a lower key.

npcs.name: Gaffer Olsen
npcs.greeting: Forty years I kept this farm. Three more since I died. The hounds don't seem to mind either way.

npcs.name: Widow Marta
npcs.greeting: My husband walks past my window every night. He doesn't knock. I leave the lamp on.

npcs.name: Acolyte Dessa
npcs.greeting: The moss on these stones isn't growing. It's feeding. I'd stay on the path.

npcs.name: Huntress Verrel
npcs.greeting: The crows don't die. They only look at you, as if you were the strange one.

npcs.name: Tobb the Farmhand
npcs.greeting: I sleep in the barn. The scarecrows don't climb the ladder, so far.

npcs.name: Gatewarden Ilsa
npcs.greeting: The Sepulcher is open to the dead. For everyone else, it is a door with a very bad temper.

npcs.name: Orchard-Warden Malwick
npcs.greeting: Malden grew the sweetest apples in Lordaeron. Now the orchard grows what it likes.

npcs.name: Webhunter Corvane
npcs.greeting: The Skittering Dark is aptly named. Keep your eyes up. The thing that gets you is never on the ground.

npcs.name: Deathguard Lyle
npcs.greeting: The Rear Guard marks the north. Past here the pines belong to whatever has the most teeth.

npcs.name: Farmer Bucklebree
npcs.greeting: Three generations on this farm. I'm the first to work it dead. I'd say the yield hasn't changed.

npcs.name: Goodwife Merriam
npcs.greeting: The hogs went first. Then the quilts. I've lost track of what's left to lose.

npcs.name: Marshwalker Thorne
npcs.greeting: Olivia's Pond was a pretty spot once. Now the water moves when nothing is stirring it.

npcs.name: Overseer Hobart
npcs.greeting: Deep Elem paid well, until it didn't. The kobolds stayed. So did I. Neither of us got a pension.

npcs.name: Field Surgeon Ashe
npcs.greeting: I stitch what's torn and I remove what's gone off. The two jobs overlap more than you'd like.

npcs.name: Hearthwarden Brand
npcs.greeting: Pyrewood burned for a reason. Whatever rose from the ashes didn't read the reasons.

npcs.name: Trapper Hask
npcs.greeting: Traps still work on the dead. They just have to be bigger.

npcs.name: Packbreaker Rynn
npcs.greeting: A pack leader is a promise to the pack. I intend to break a few promises.

npcs.name: Corporal Teague
npcs.greeting: The Wall's been shut since the night the gate fell. We don't open it. We don't let anything open it.

npcs.name: Millwright Haskell
npcs.greeting: Ambermill ran on Dalaran gold and Dalaran sawdust. Now it runs on ghosts and spite.

npcs.name: Magister Orsolo
npcs.greeting: The waygate was a mill-lift, once. Then someone aimed it somewhere worse.

npcs.name: Ferryman Gael
npcs.greeting: The boat goes where the lake lets it. Pay up front. The lake keeps a tally.

npcs.name: Dockhand Pim
npcs.greeting: Crates wash up all hours. Half of them are empty. The other half I don't open.

npcs.name: Gatekeeper Marl
npcs.greeting: Behind that portcullis is Shadowfang Keep. If you hear howling, it's the draught. Say it's the draught.

npcs.name: Commander Halvard Vane
npcs.greeting: The Sepulcher holds the north-west of Silverpine. The dead have taken to it better than the living ever did.

npcs.name: Adjutant Kess
npcs.greeting: The Commander speaks to you, or he doesn't. Either way, stand up straight. Not that it matters.

npcs.name: Pier-Warden Hask
npcs.greeting: The ferry leaves when the lake lets it. If you're staying, stay off the water. It remembers the crossing.

npcs.name: Scout Merrin
npcs.greeting: Baron Ashbury's manor sits behind that gate. The guards haven't been relieved since the curse. Neither has the Baron.

npcs.name: Warden Orlan
npcs.greeting: The arch in the ridge leads down to where the curse was cast. I keep watch so nothing climbs back up.

npcs.name: Gravehunter Selke
npcs.greeting: Cur's Grave is a kennel for ghosts. The dogs I can handle. It's the keeper I don't like the sound of.

npcs.name: Bat Handler Skrel
npcs.greeting: The bats don't mind the smell down here. They're the only ones. Where to?

npcs.name: Bat Handler Mirren
npcs.greeting: Fed, saddled and only mildly hungry for you. Name your destination.

npcs.name: Bat Handler Odo
npcs.greeting: Fly the Rearguard's route and you'll never see the Dalaran wall from the ground. Where to?

npcs.name: Bat Handler Veshka
npcs.greeting: Forest roads are for the careless. Hold the straps and pick a roost.

npcs.name: Gate Guard Hollis
npcs.greeting: South gate. State your business, keep to the road, and do not swim the race.

npcs.name: Watchman Grell
npcs.greeting: Three bridges, three of us. You would be amazed how many try the water anyway.

npcs.name: Miller Aldous Reed
npcs.greeting: The wheel has turned every day for sixty years. Who holds the town has never once stopped it.

npcs.name: Stablemaster Brann Teague
npcs.greeting: Horses will not cross the bridges at night. Clever animals, horses.

npcs.name: Farrier Nell Marsh
npcs.greeting: Hooves and hinges. Half this town runs on things I hammered flat.

npcs.name: Chaplain Ewen Blackwood
npcs.greeting: I keep the chapel on this side. They have never asked me to stop. I have never asked why.

npcs.name: Sluice-Keeper Pate
npcs.greeting: Crank's mine. Drop the gate and the wheel stops, the vats go cold, and everyone remembers my name.

npcs.name: Farmhand Dorrin
npcs.greeting: Barley in the north plots, oats in the south. Same as my mother sowed, same rows.

npcs.name: Apprentice Nilla Stitch
npcs.greeting: I label everything. If a jar has no label, do not open it, and do not tell me you opened it.

npcs.name: Commander Vellis Thorne
npcs.greeting: Alterac to the north, Southshore to the south, and the Syndicate in between. We hold the middle.

npcs.name: Scout Mirren Vask
npcs.greeting: Durnholde is thick with Syndicate and the hills are thick with gnolls. Walk the road.

npcs.name: Commander Hale Rethven
npcs.greeting: One tower, and every farm in the valley watching it. We hold what we can see from the top.

npcs.name: Apothecary Jessel Vane
npcs.greeting: Green country. Do you know how long it has been since I had anything LIVING to work with?

npcs.name: Deathguard Orlin
npcs.greeting: Militia come up the road twice a week to look at us. We look back. Nobody has swung yet.

npcs.name: Scout Aelin Frost
npcs.greeting: You came down out of Silverpine. Take a breath - the air here does not have the blight in it.

npcs.name: Outrider Kess
npcs.greeting: East road runs to Tarren Mill. Stay on it. What is off it is not friendly and not slow.

npcs.name: Agent Sarra Dunwick
npcs.greeting: The farmhands out here still think this is their valley. I am not in a hurry to correct them.

npcs.name: Poacher Tam Hollis
npcs.greeting: I take a ram now and then. The Marshal calls it theft. The rams have no opinion.

npcs.name: Scout Bren Ashby
npcs.greeting: Count the militia, count the marines, report, repeat. Riveting work.

npcs.name: Herder Maud Kellen
npcs.greeting: Yetis come down off the snowline when it turns cold. My rams know it before I do.

npcs.name: Overseer Grint Halloway
npcs.greeting: Azurelode was the richest silver seam in the valley. Now it is the wettest.

npcs.name: Surveyor Pell Iversen
npcs.greeting: I mapped those workings before they flooded. The map is worth more than the mine now.

npcs.name: Tidewatcher Nols
npcs.greeting: Murlocs on the strand, and something further out that the murlocs are frightened of.

npcs.name: Spy Lia Marrow
npcs.greeting: Southshore is awake, armed, and three hundred strong. Walk in and you will not walk out.

npcs.name: Forager Ned Quill
npcs.greeting: Apples the size of your fist, and wasps the size of your hand guarding every one of them.

npcs.name: Castaway Ilsa Roane
npcs.greeting: My ship went down off that shore. Everyone else who came up out of the water came up wrong.

npcs.name: Saboteur Henk
npcs.greeting: Dey build a dock, I burn a dock. Simple arrangement. Works fine.

npcs.name: Magistrate Orrin Pell
npcs.greeting: Everything east of the mill is my problem: gnolls, Syndicate, ogres, and a wall nobody can open.

npcs.name: Field Apothecary Wren
npcs.greeting: I sample the ditches so the ones inside the town do not have to. It is a career.

npcs.name: Deathguard Kolt
npcs.greeting: Gate's behind me, road's in front of you. Mind which one you are facing when you draw.

npcs.name: Caravan Master Ovid Thane
npcs.greeting: Flour out, reagents in, twice a month. The Syndicate has started taking an interest in my wheels.

npcs.name: Huntsman Dell Varrow
npcs.greeting: Worgs in the hedgerows, gnolls in the hollow. I was a gamekeeper. Now I am a different sort.

npcs.name: Scout Pria Halm
npcs.greeting: West road to the Foothills, east road to everything that wants you dead. Choose carefully.

npcs.name: Trapper Gus Mirren
npcs.greeting: Mudsnout gnolls took my whole line of snares and left me the stakes. Insulting, that.

npcs.name: Outrider Jace
npcs.greeting: I ride the west road all day and most of the night. It has never once been quiet.

npcs.name: Infiltrator Vess
npcs.greeting: Gavin's Naze is a fence's camp with delusions. Everything stolen in this valley passes through it.

npcs.name: Watcher Odrin Falk
npcs.greeting: The keep has been held by the Syndicate longer than it was ever held by Lordaeron. Think on that.

npcs.name: Scholar Emeline Vask
npcs.greeting: Thrall was kept in that keep as a boy. Half the Horde's history started behind those walls.

npcs.name: Outrider Brann Odgar
npcs.greeting: Nethander ogres took da stead. Dey took da barn too, and dey are living in it.

npcs.name: Sapper Niall Crag
npcs.greeting: Dwarves cut that fort square into the ridge. I have been told to find a way in that is not the door.

npcs.name: Tidewatcher Ferris
npcs.greeting: Daggerspine murlocs on this strand too. They are spreading, and nobody will say from where.

npcs.name: Sentry Ada Rook
npcs.greeting: Thoradin's Wall. Built by an empire that is dust, and it still closes the road.

npcs.name: Gate-Warden Vessaria
npcs.greeting: Name, business, and whether you intend to take anything out. The third one is the question that matters.

npcs.name: Porter Dunhal
npcs.greeting: Blood elves everywhere and one of me. They needed somebody who does not mind the dark and does not need to breathe.

npcs.name: Stable-Hand Corwin
npcs.greeting: Nothing stabled here was born here. They do not like the ceiling. Neither do I, and I have had three years.

npcs.name: Cartographer Elandrin
npcs.greeting: Fourth full survey. The first three disagree with each other and with this one, and the cavern is not moving. I have checked.

npcs.name: Naturalist Orienne
npcs.greeting: Everyone calls the fungus scenery. The fungus is the largest single organism any of us has ever stood on, and nobody will fund me.

npcs.name: Enchanter Vaelios
npcs.greeting: The ambient arcane here does half my work and I do not know what it wants in return. Probably nothing. Probably.

npcs.name: Magister Saeltheris
npcs.greeting: We are not colonists. We are cataloguers. The distinction is important to me and to nobody else.

npcs.name: Archivist Nessaly
npcs.greeting: You arrived the same year we did, which the Codex finds easier to ignore than to address. I do not ignore things.

npcs.name: Codex-Master Ilarien Duskwaking
npcs.greeting: Three years, eleven thousand entries, and one cavern that keeps producing things I have no column for. Welcome to the Crimson Codex.

npcs.name: Adjutant Pell
npcs.greeting: The Codex-Master will see you. She sees everyone. It is the filing afterwards that takes the time.

npcs.name: Hall-Sentinel Durannis
npcs.greeting: They hired me because I do not care what the crystal says. Three years on, I still do not.

npcs.name: Watcher Kaelen Mornstride
npcs.greeting: Everyone stops here. Three years and I have not met one person who walked out of that passage without stopping.

npcs.name: Surveyor Aelwyn
npcs.greeting: I map the far wall from here because there is no closer place to stand. That should tell you something about the scale.

npcs.name: Harvester Delvin Brightsunder
npcs.greeting: Shardfields work. Hard on the hands, hard on the eyes, and the Codex counts every crate.

npcs.name: Surveyor Pelorien
npcs.greeting: It grows in exact repeating figures. Geology does not do that. I have been told to write 'unusual mineralisation' and I have written it.

npcs.name: Naturalist Imrelle
npcs.greeting: The water is lit from underneath and the light keeps time with the Lumen. Ask me what that means and I will tell you honestly that I do not know.

npcs.name: Scholar Veridan
npcs.greeting: Dalaran masonry. Two hundred spans underground, in a cavern that is three years old. Nobody carried it down.

npcs.name: Overseer Thaleon Greyquill
npcs.greeting: The Archive is the reason we are all still here, and the reason half of us want to leave.

npcs.name: Digger Sarenne
npcs.greeting: I shift rock and they file what comes out. Last week what came out had a Codex catalogue number on it that we have not issued yet.

npcs.name: Scout Rhennik
npcs.greeting: The Lumen does not reach past that ridge. Everything I know about what does live out there, I learned at a run.

npcs.name: Bloom-Warden Ysolde Emberquill
npcs.greeting: There is something growing down there in the shape of a library. The Codex wants it read. I want it burned. We have been arguing for eleven months.

npcs.name: Forager Mikael
npcs.greeting: The caps are safe, the stalks are not, and the ones that look like faces are fine. I have eaten all three so you do not have to.

npcs.name: Scout Garuk Emberhide
npcs.greeting: Warchief wants to know what we border now. I have been here a season and my answer is still 'a mountain', which he will not like.

npcs.name: Keeper Nalu Stillgrass
npcs.greeting: I kept the winch on this side for eleven years. The cable still runs out thirty feet and into granite, and I still come up here and look at it.

npcs.name: Watcher Tomak Redhoof
npcs.greeting: Stand with your left foot in red dust and your right in leaf mould. The line is that sharp. Nothing grew across it. Nothing is going to.

npcs.name: Fizzik Quickline
npcs.greeting: Four ways down off this rim and three of them kill you. I sell rope. You see the opportunity here, I can tell by your face.

npcs.name: Runner Ash Winterfall
npcs.greeting: I take the chutes. Everyone tells me not to. They are the only ground up here that stays swept, and a swept path is a fast path if you are not slow.

npcs.name: Hesta Coldshoulder
npcs.greeting: Something is melting up here and I would like to know how fast. The creek at the bottom runs higher every spring and nobody downstream has worked out why.

npcs.name: Elder Mura Longstand
npcs.greeting: We were plains people a very short time ago. Now I can tell you which of these trees will split clean and which will fight you, and I would rather not have learned it.

npcs.name: Hateg Barkhand
npcs.greeting: Aspen is not oak and it is not kodo-grass. Green it is heavy and wet, seasoned it is light as nothing. Everything we knew about wood was about a different wood.

npcs.name: Hunter Sani Quietstep
npcs.greeting: Elk up here are bigger than anything on the plain and they do not run the same. You lose them in timber. I never once lost anything on open ground.

npcs.name: Scout Owen Tallgrass
npcs.greeting: Elkhorn is the only place in this zone you can see anything. Everywhere else is trees and the trees are all the same trees. I come up here to remember what distance looks like.

npcs.name: Warden Gelt Rivermane
npcs.greeting:
The beavers had this valley before we did and they have done more with it. Every pond on these benches is theirs. We just walk between them.

You came off that blue world, didn't you. Do they have beavers there? Nobody can ever tell me.

npcs.name: Warden Hesk Stonefoot
npcs.greeting: Everything that reaches this town comes up that ramp and across this rock. Including you, so you will forgive me for looking.

npcs.name: Bridge-Keeper Oda
npcs.greeting: I check every rope on all three spans, every morning, before anyone crosses. It takes two hours. I have never once been asked to do it and I am never going to stop.

npcs.name: Innkeeper Tamu
npcs.greeting: First night up here nobody sleeps. The wind comes under the floor and you lie there doing arithmetic about rope. Second night you sleep fine. I do not know why and I have stopped asking.

npcs.name: Skywatcher Rell
npcs.greeting: From the lookout you can see the aspen on a clear day - a dark line along the north, where the mountain starts. Three years ago that was sky.

npcs.name: Totem-Keeper Ashti
npcs.greeting: The great totem is aspen. Pale wood, wrong wood, carried down out of a range that is not from here. The spirits have not objected. I asked for a long time before I stopped.

npcs.name: Wind-Rider Kalo
npcs.greeting: Only road in is the ramp, and the ramp is slow. Everything in a hurry comes to me.

npcs.name: Caravan-Master Bohl
npcs.greeting: Four caravans a week up that ramp and not one of them on time. The road is fine. It is the ramp. It is always the ramp.

npcs.name: Stablemaster Reth
npcs.greeting: Kodo do not cross rope bridges. They learned that before we did, and one of them was right the first time.

npcs.name: Wrangler Umak
npcs.greeting: They pen up here because up here is where the ramp ends. Anything with four legs lives on this top its whole life and never sees the rest of the city.

npcs.name: Sentry Palla
npcs.greeting: One road in. That is the whole defence and it is a better one than Thunder Bluff had.

npcs.name: High Elder Namka Windhollow
npcs.greeting:
Longtread will not come. He has refused the seat and he has refused this city, and he is right to, and I have stopped arguing about it.

So it is me. We built this. That is the part I cannot get used to - we built something again.

npcs.name: MerchantTusk
npcs.greeting: Dere is only one bank, mon, and dere is only one me. Do not ask how dat works. Hand me ya things and go be a hero.

npcs.name: Auctioneer Mott
npcs.greeting: Everything sold here was carried up a ramp, so everything here is priced like it was carried up a ramp. People complain. People also pay.

npcs.name: Healer Ilna Softstep
npcs.greeting: Falls, mostly. Not off the edge - nobody falls off the edge, people are careful about the edge. Off ladders. Always off ladders.

npcs.name: The Rememberer
npcs.greeting: I hold the names. Everyone who was in the city when the ground took it, in order, and I say them through once a season. It takes most of a night. I am not going to stop doing that either.

npcs.name: Tanner Yula
npcs.greeting: Hide, leather and cloth, same bench. Bring me something that was recently an animal and we will get along.

npcs.name: Timberwright Gohn
npcs.greeting: Every plank in this city came off a mountain that was not here three years ago. I have stopped finding that strange, which I am told is the strange part.

npcs.name: Bowyer Tesh
npcs.greeting: Aspen takes a bend and holds it. Nothing on the plain did that. I am building better bows than my mother did and I would rather she were here to be annoyed about it.

npcs.name: Carver Oyat
npcs.greeting: Pale wood. Wrong wood. It carves like a dream and I have never once got used to the colour.

npcs.name: Potter Hesha
npcs.greeting: Clay comes up the ramp in sacks. Everything comes up the ramp. If you ever want to understand this city, stand at the bottom of the ramp for a day.

npcs.name: Spirit-Walker Enu
npcs.greeting: The dead of Thunder Bluff are not restless. I have looked. Whatever took the city did not take them with it, and that is the only comfort I have been able to find in three years of looking.

npcs.name: Elder Grasswind
npcs.greeting: We meet on this top because it is the only ground up here with room for all of us. That is the whole reason. People read a great deal more into it.

npcs.name: Elder Tarn Blackhoof
npcs.greeting: Half the council wants to go back to Mulgore and half knows what is in Mulgore now. I sit between them and say very little, and that is considered wisdom.

npcs.name: Lookout Sima
npcs.greeting: Highest standing ground in Thousand Needles. I can see weather three days out. I cannot see home, and I have tried.

npcs.name: MerchantTusk
npcs.greeting: Dere is only one bank, mon, and dere is only one me. Do not ask how dat works. Hand me ya things and go be a hero.

npcs.name: Overseer Mokra
npcs.greeting: The camp holds. That is the whole of my report and it has been for three years.

npcs.name: Berth-Master Zekka
npcs.greeting: Everything you see here came off that airship. Including me.

npcs.name: Signalman Grut
npcs.greeting: Two flags means they are coming in. Three means they are not stopping.

npcs.name: Scout Hanzo
npcs.greeting: I have walked as far south as the seam and back. I do not recommend the walk.

npcs.name: Drillmaster Ukko
npcs.greeting: Half of them have never fought anything that climbs.

npcs.name: Sentry Vrak
npcs.greeting: Road's that way. Keep to it and the jungle mostly keeps to itself.

npcs.name: Runner Teza
npcs.greeting: I made it back. Took the long way round the fen and I would do it again.

npcs.name: Field-Medic Sulaa
npcs.greeting: Bring them to me standing if you can. Bring them to me either way.

npcs.name: Mapmaker Ashi
npcs.greeting: The map is wrong. It is less wrong than it was. That is the job.

npcs.name: Attaché Zul'jana
npcs.greeting: You all keep calling it a jungle. It has a name. Several.

npcs.name: Storesman Pell
npcs.greeting: Count it in, count it out. The jungle takes what it wants in between.

npcs.name: Beast-Handler Kozza
npcs.greeting: They are not tame. They are fed. There is a difference and I respect it.

npcs.name: Smith Dorgun
npcs.greeting: Damp eats steel faster than any enemy I ever met.

npcs.name: Baron Revilgaz
npcs.greeting: Nothing leaves this cove without my name on it. Not even you.

npcs.name: Aide Fipple
npcs.greeting: The Baron is reviewing it. The Baron is always reviewing it.

npcs.name: Tollkeeper Nizzik
npcs.greeting: Landing fee. You have already landed, so we are only arguing about the amount.

npcs.name: Harbourmaster Sprocket
npcs.greeting: Tide, berth, weather, and who is lying about which. That is the whole tower.

npcs.name: Bruiser Kolk
npcs.greeting: Trouble on the quay is my trouble. Trouble up here is yours.

npcs.name: Lookout Minzi
npcs.greeting: Clear to the cape. Which only means I cannot see them yet.

npcs.name: Dockmaster Brek
npcs.greeting: Three piers, one crane, and everybody wants the middle one.

npcs.name: Crane-Hand Durgo
npcs.greeting: Stand under it once and you will not do it twice.

npcs.name: Shipwright Vella
npcs.greeting: Salt, worm and rot. Pick two and I can still float it.

npcs.name: Factor Weezel
npcs.greeting: The port has not left the company. I have the paperwork. Nobody reads it.

npcs.name: The Quiet Man
npcs.greeting: I did not see you come in and I will not see you leave.

npcs.name: Dagger-Hand Oona
npcs.greeting: They have not hanged me and they have not let me go. Make of that what you like.

npcs.name: Pilot Zan'rek
npcs.greeting: The reef moves. Not fast. Fast enough.

npcs.name: Scrip
npcs.greeting: Carry your crate? Watch your crate? Both is cheaper.

npcs.name: Innkeeper Rukha
npcs.greeting: Twelve bunks and a fire. Set your hearth here and the jungle stops being a one-way trip.

npcs.name: Windrider-Keeper Pazzik
npcs.greeting: Only one other roost worth flying to from here, and the Baron charges me to land on it.

npcs.name: Girzzik Vaultkeep
npcs.greeting: The vault is under the waterline and it has never flooded. Think about that.
npcs._source: Was bootybay_banker, a goblin with is_banker set and the name MerchantTusk. Two standing rules said it could not stay: Kyle's 'major cities only should have bankers' (Booty Bay is not one), and MerchantTusk is ONE recurring character - the troll banker in Orgrimmar, Undercity and Freewind Post - so a goblin wearing his name read as a continuity error rather than a second banker. Kept as a plain Booty Bay local instead of deleted, because the greeting is authored flavour worth keeping and Booty Bay having someone who talks about a vault is fine; there is simply no bank to use. Renamed so MerchantTusk stays the troll. Fixed 5 Nov 2026.

npcs.name: Wind-Rider Zekki
npcs.greeting: North to the camp, and that is the whole map. Nobody flies out of this jungle.

npcs.name: Wind-Rider Ghulrak
npcs.greeting: Hillsbrad from the air is all fences. You do not see how much of it is fences until you are over it.

npcs.name: Skyward-Warden Thalyn
npcs.greeting: The fissure is wide enough to fly out of. Getting a hippogryph to agree took most of a season.

npcs.name: Wind-Rider Aleris
npcs.greeting: Astranaar inland, and nothing else from here. The coast road is for people with time.

npcs.name: Innkeeper Lysaia
npcs.greeting: Four beds and a fire that does not go out. It is not much, but it is dry and it is the last one west.

npcs.name: Road-Ganger Dubo
npcs.greeting: Road's cut as far as the ford. After the ford it is cut as far as I was paid to.

npcs.name: Tout Bexxil
npcs.greeting: You are on the board already. You were on it before you got here.

npcs.name: Gatehouse Broker Zul'tamo
npcs.greeting: The ring runs one way. That is not a custom. That is masonry.

npcs.name: Ordek Fenn
npcs.greeting: Sit down, sit down. I have not had anyone to be wrong at in weeks.

npcs.name: Netsetter Ulua
npcs.greeting: Nets are set. Nets have been set since before you were a rumour.

npcs.name: Watcher Garza
npcs.greeting: One road up and I am sitting on it. Write that down, it is the whole post.

npcs.name: Barkeep Snod
npcs.greeting: Vozzi runs the beds. I run the bar. We have not spoken in two years and the business has never been better, so do not fix it.

npcs.name: Race-Marshal Tozzik Brasswheel
npcs.greeting:
The Saltwheel Open runs the first clear day after the winter wet. Entries at the gantry, scrutineering at noon, flag at two.

Nobody has entered for three seasons. I post the times anyway. Somebody has to hold the date or the date goes away, and then what is this.

npcs.name: Pit-Boss Grizzik Vane
npcs.greeting: I keep four hands on the payroll for a race that has not run since the Integration. Tozzik pays half, I pay half, and neither of us has said out loud what we are paying for.

npcs.name: Old Nazzik
npcs.greeting:
Course record. Mine. Eleven years and nobody has touched it.

That is because nobody has driven the course in three, which I am aware of, and which does not take the record off me.

npcs.name: Tally-Clerk Winnow
npcs.greeting: Every cart in, every cart out, every barrel of salt, written down twice. The town is shrinking and I can tell you by exactly how much, which makes me the least popular person in it.

npcs.name: Watcher Brak Kesh
npcs.greeting:
Five mounds I can see from this fence. Three years ago there were two, and the near one was twice as far out as it is now.

I say the number every evening in the inn. They have started buying me drinks so I will say it quieter.

npcs.name: Doc Pellik
npcs.greeting: Salt sores, sun, and whatever the bugs do to a hand. Three complaints, in that order, every season, and I could do the whole job in my sleep if the third one would stop climbing.

npcs.name: Harbourmaster Senna Coil
npcs.greeting:
Four berths, and I have been turning ships away since the second winter.

They want me to cut two more out of the rock. I have told them what that costs and they have told me what the waiting costs and we are both right, which is the most annoying way for an argument to be stuck.

npcs.name: Wind-Rider Kezzik
npcs.greeting:
Only bird for a very long way, and I price like it.

Folk come off that pan on foot with a face on them and ask why there is no post out there. There IS a post out there. There is no BIRD on it, because a bird needs feeding and a feeding needs somebody paying, and six customers do not pay for a wyvern.

I would love to be wrong. Bring me the town that makes me wrong.

npcs.name: Barkeep Oll
npcs.greeting:
Quay side of the room is quiet and the yard side is not, and I have stopped trying to seat anybody anywhere.

They drink together. That is the thing nobody says out loud when they are telling you how divided this town is. They argue in here and then they go to work in the morning on the same dock.

npcs.name: Yard-Boss Grizzel Hack
npcs.greeting:
Everything that is not on a ship or in a shop is on my yard, and most of what IS on a ship came off it.

Three years ago this was a goat field and I was somebody's third-best foreman in a town with a wall round it. Now I am this. I think about that most mornings for about as long as it takes to get my boots on.

npcs.name: Old Mazzic
npcs.greeting:
I did not leave Gadgetzan. Everybody says left. I was carried out on a door by two people whose names I never got.

So when the quay crowd say we ARRIVED, like it was a thing we decided on a Tuesday - no. Some of us arrived. The rest of us were brought.

npcs.name: Tally-Clerk Hesper Dunn
npcs.greeting:
Every crate in, every crate out, which side of town it came from and which side it went to.

People assume I keep the last two columns to be unpleasant. I keep them because in four years somebody is going to claim this town was always like this, and I would like to be able to put a book on the table.

npcs.name: Surgeon Wick Ambrose
npcs.greeting:
Crush injuries, mostly. A dock does that to people - a rope goes, or a load swings, or somebody puts a hand where a hand has no business being.

I have treated more of the yard crowd than the quay crowd and it is not because they are careless. It is because they are the ones doing the lifting, and if anybody tells you different send them to me.

npcs.name: Dig-Boss Marn Cobble
npcs.greeting:
Eleven months. Eleven months of paying ninety people's wages out of a hole producing nothing, and do you know what the ledger in Steamwheedle calls that? It calls it MY FAULT.

It was not my fault. We were four hundred feet down a clean seam when the water came up to meet us, and water does not come UP. Not here. Not in a desert.

And before you say it - yes, I have heard the theory that it started when the worlds got stitched together. Everyone's problem started when the worlds got stitched together. Mine came with a figure attached.

npcs.name: Pump-Chief Grizzik Thane
npcs.greeting:
Six pumps. Four of them are mine and two of them are the Survey's, and the two that are the Survey's are the two that work, which I would like entered into a record somewhere.

I can clear the first gallery in nine days. I have been able to clear the first gallery in nine days for eleven months. All I need is for two people who both think they are the adult here to say the same sentence out loud on the same afternoon.

npcs.name: Tally-Clerk Oss Pinch
npcs.greeting:
Nine hundred and forty-one days of water level, taken at dawn, written down whether anybody wanted it or not.

The Boss says my book proves the flood is seasonal. Ulla says my book proves the flood is not. It is the SAME BOOK. I have started to suspect that a number is only ever worth what the person reading it already believed, which is a terrible thing for a clerk to work out about herself.

npcs.name: Ulla Stormhollow
npcs.greeting:
I started at the Aspen melt four years ago because the thaw was coming early and nobody could tell me why.

Then the Needles went dry. Then the pan went to salt. Then a walled city out east died of thirst with a well in the middle of it, and then the floor of the desert fell in, and at every single one of those places somebody told me it was a local problem with a local cause.

It is one problem. You are standing in it. Every drop of water that left those five places is in this pool, and water does not CHOOSE to go somewhere. It goes where it is pulled.

So. Something down that shaft has been drinking a region for three years, and the goblins want to open the door and ask it for the crystal.

npcs.name: Diver Sanna Creel
npcs.greeting:
Forty feet in on a lungful, tie off, forty feet back. I have been into the first gallery nine times and I have come out nine times, which I am aware is not the same as being good at it.

It is not dark in there. That is the part nobody writes down. There is light coming off the seam and it is not the colour that crystal goes when you put a lamp on it. It is the colour crystal goes when something is USING it.

npcs.name: Chief Surveyor Peska Vane
npcs.greeting:
This is Fourth Peg. The peg's stood seven months, which is longer than the other three did.

The first fell in with the ground under it. The second's on the lip of the Wide Sink, marking ground that's gone. We moved the third because Hask didn't like the hardpan, and that spot fell in four days later.

The port at Steamwheedle pays me to find out if a road can be built across the Abyssal Sands. I don't know yet.

npcs.name: Rodman Hask Quill
npcs.greeting:
I'm the one who stands at the far end holding the staff. Out here the far end's usually somewhere nobody's walked before.

I like the work. I know that sounds odd.

You can read this ground if you go slowly. The hardpan sounds different over a hollow, and it's louder on a cold morning. Peska wants that written up as a method. Every time I try, it reads like guessing.

npcs.name: Teamster Odd Varrow
npcs.greeting:
I was driving the second cart at Nineteen Mile when the road went. The lead pair were six lengths ahead of me.

The cart went down and I fell off the back, and the ground I landed on held. I didn't do anything clever. I've told that story four hundred times.

I could hear the lead pair down there for a day and a half. So when the camp talks about the ground like it's weather, I go and stand somewhere else.

npcs.name: Rope-Hand Vizzi Trask
npcs.greeting:
Somebody has to go down the pits on a rope and see if there's a floor. That's me.

Nine of the eleven have floors. The Throats in the southwest and Underlight in the southeast don't, as far as my line reaches.

Peska writes those up as 'no bottom observed'. I'd write 'don't go down'.

npcs.name: Commander Zel Raskal
npcs.greeting: Two years on this moor. We hold the road, the wall and this pile of somebody else's masonry, and I have stopped asking Orgrimmar for a third thing.

npcs.name: Scout Grim Hollowfoot
npcs.greeting: The moor looks empty. It is not empty. It is just very good at being wide.

npcs.name: Warden Ada Rook
npcs.greeting: I stood at this gap for a year and a half before anyone came through it, and then it was you. Go on, then. It is open.

npcs.name: Antiquarian Vesh
npcs.greeting: Stromgarde is a ruin with a ruin under it. The Syndicate is squatting in the upper one and has not noticed the stair.

npcs.name: Shepherd Ogrin
npcs.greeting: Somebody has to keep the stag herd off the road, and it turns out somebody is me. I was an axethrower. Ask me about it and I will tell you at length.

npcs.name: Nalla Deeps
npcs.greeting: Go'Shek Farm still brings in a harvest. The Syndicate took the farm, not the farming, and somebody is buying the grain. I am interested in who.

npcs.name: Overlord Gath'rok
npcs.greeting: Hammerfall holds the middle of this region and the middle is the only part that matters. Everything that crosses Arathi crosses in front of me.

npcs.name: Sergeant Mok Blackstone
npcs.greeting: Drill at dawn, wall at noon, drill again. The ogres come up out of the hold every few weeks and find us standing in the same place, which is the entire idea.

npcs.name: Stablemaster Rukka
npcs.greeting: Kodo on the left, wolves on the right, and never the other way round. I learned that the hard way and the kodo learned it harder.

npcs.name: Apothecary Dellwyn Voss
npcs.greeting: The mere water in the basin has something living in it. I have written four reports. Undercity has acknowledged receipt of three.

npcs.name: Deathguard Olen
npcs.greeting: I watch the east gate. Everything that has come through it in two years has been kobold, ogre, or a man with a very good reason, and the third kind is the problem.

npcs.name: High Envoy Tamka Stillwater
npcs.greeting: The stone rings in this basin were raised by people who are gone, and the ogres are taking them down for wall stone. I have asked twice. I will ask a third time.

npcs.name: Scholar Innik Barrowmouth
npcs.greeting: Four circles, one line, and the line is the road - which means the road is older than anyone who has ever walked it, including the people who think they built it.

npcs.name: Prospector Thugg
npcs.greeting: Drywhisker was a mine before the kobolds got it and it is a mine now. The difference is that the kobolds dug past the ore.

npcs.name: Runner Keska
npcs.greeting: Refuge Pointe to Hammerfall and back, twice a week, on foot, because wyverns are for officers. Ask me what the road is doing and I will actually know.

npcs.name: Bosun Kaz Tidewright
npcs.greeting: I am a bosun running a shore camp, which is not a job that exists. Orgrimmar sent four boats and no officer, so here we are and here I am.

npcs.name: Shipwright Oona Keelsplice
npcs.greeting: Every hull on this archipelago is on the rocks and I can see six of them from where I am standing. Give me a crew and a tide and I will give you two of them back.

npcs.name: Scout Vel Ashgrave
npcs.greeting: The Bloodsail are not raiding. They are holding. There is a difference and the difference is that holding means they want something that is already here.

npcs.name: Barrow-Watcher Yelza
npcs.greeting: Dat barrow full of Arathor dead and dey still standin' watch. Three t'ousand years. Nobody told dem de job was over, an' I not goin' in dere to say it.

npcs.name: The Bothy Hermit
npcs.greeting: I was on the ferry. Then the water was a different water and the ferry was on a rock, and that was three years ago, and this is my rock now.

npcs.name: Trainer Garrek
npcs.greeting: I have taught every one of the disciplines at one time or another, and I am not precious about which you picked. Show me where you are and bring gold.

npcs.name: Trainer Drogan

npcs.name: Bosun Grekka Sparfall
npcs.greeting:
Welcome to Ashclaim Landing. Watch your step on the jetty, some of the planks are loose.

I run the jetty and the boat to Saltspur. The Thane's old city is under the hill to the south-east, and the town is round the far side of the volcano. Most of the work here is getting things from one to the other.

npcs.name: Surveyor Pim Brackwhistle
npcs.greeting:
I'm surveying this island for the underwriters. Every tree, every seam of ore and every hole in the ground needs a value written down.

My cousin Nix holds the Ashclaim's paper in Cinderwharf. I do the walking.

npcs.name: Gatewatch Bron Emberhold
npcs.greeting:
That arch is the front gate of Khaz Varun. My family kept it for nine generations before the city went dark.

The Thane has me here to count who goes in and who comes out. I've never been inside myself.

npcs.name: Prospector Hesta Ironwick
npcs.greeting:
This is good ground for ore. There's mithril near the surface and truesilver if you know what rock to look for.

The gorillas keep throwing my samples back at me, so it's slow work.

npcs.name: Tidewalker Jex
npcs.greeting:
The water's only waist deep all the way out to the last rock, so you can walk to most of the wrecks.

A lot of them still have cargo on board. I'd go out myself, but the crabs took my boots.

npcs.name: Thane Durgan Ashhold
npcs.greeting:
I'm Durgan Ashhold, Thane of Khaz Varun.

My great-grandfather's hall is under the south shore, and it's full of what's left of my family. The Underwriter pays for the work. I want the hall cleared and my people laid to rest.

npcs.name: Keeper Morn Ashhold
npcs.greeting:
I keep a flame on this terrace for everyone who's still down in the city.

My cousin Durgan is the Thane. He looks after the claim and I look after the dead.

npcs.name: Underwriter Nix Brackwhistle
npcs.greeting:
I hold the paper on the Ashclaim, which means my partners paid for all of this.

The Thane wants his ancestors laid to rest and I want a working foundry. Both need the same doors opened, so we work well enough together.

npcs.name: Wind Rider Keeper Zazzi
npcs.greeting:
The pad is out over the water so the wind from the wings doesn't damage the roofs.

I can fly you to Saltspur whenever you like, and you can get anywhere from there.

npcs.name: Artifact Keeper Morgha
npcs.greeting: The same hands made every version of your set. Leave the piece with me and take the one that suits how you fight now. No charge. Keepers do not sell.

npcs.name: Artifact Keeper Lenore Vance
npcs.greeting: The same hands made every version of your set. Leave the piece with me and take the one that suits how you fight now. No charge. Keepers do not sell.

npcs.greeting: The same hands made every version of your set. Leave the piece with me and take the one that suits how you fight now. No charge. Keepers do not sell.
